findings.issue_text: [BUG] `get_merged_pr_single_issue_template` calls `PRCommentWorkflow._truncate_title(title)` but no class named `PRCommentWorkflow` exists in commit_context.py (the class is `PullRequestCommentWorkflow`, and `_truncate_title` is defined on `CommitContextIntegration`), causing a NameError on every merged-PR comment render via GitHub/Gitlab `get_comment_body`; fix by calling `CommitContextIntegration._truncate_title`

[ADVISORY] Neutered migrations 0917 and 0920 reference `0921_convert_org_saved_searches_to_views_rerevised.py` as the correct migration, but no such file appears in the diff, risking a no-op conversion chain where org saved-search to GroupSearchView conversion silently never happens

[ADVISORY] `fetch_error_details` zips `error_ids` against `events.values()` from `nodestore.backend.get_multi`, silently assuming backend ordering; reordered or missing keys would misalign event_id with data and attribute errors to the wrong event in Seer summaries — iterate with `events.items()` instead

[BUG] Neither `age` nor `timestamp` is required on `BrowserReportSerializer`, so a report containing neither passes validation, but the Reporting API spec requires exactly one of the two; the mutual-exclusion validators only fire when both are present, leaving the 'neither present' case unhandled, so reports with no time information are silently accepted and logged as `browser_report_received`

[BUG] `BROWSER_REPORT_TYPES` ChoiceField hard-rejects any unlisted type with 422 and the list omits types Chrome actually sends (e.g. `nelson`), so valid browser submissions are rejected wholesale; one invalid report in the array returns 422 for the entire batch, dropping valid reports alongside it (no partial acceptance)

[BUG] `validate_timestamp` uses `if self.initial_data.get("age")`, so `age: 0` is falsy and bypasses the mutual-exclusion check — a report with both `age: 0` and a `timestamp` is accepted, violating the exactly-one invariant; same falsy check in `validate_age` for `timestamp: 0`

[ADVISORY] `user_agent = serializers.CharField()` is required, but `user_agent` is optional (SHOULD, not MUST) in the editor's draft of the Reporting spec; browsers/proxies that omit it will get 422 where the previous dataclass would have accepted the report, rejecting legitimate report traffic at ingest

[BUG] `fetch_error_details` uses `zip(error_ids, events.values())` pairing error IDs positionally with nodestore `get_multi` results, but `get_multi` returns only found nodes; if any node is missing, every subsequent pairing shifts so error ID `X` is reported with event `Y`'s content in the replay summary sent to Seer — must iterate `events[node_id]` per `event_id`

[BUG] `get_merged_pr_single_issue_template`, `get_environment_info`, and `_truncate_title` are added as methods of `CommitContextIntegration`, but call sites invoke them via `self` from `GitHubPRCommentWorkflow`/`GitlabPRCommentWorkflow` mixins that don't inherit from `CommitContextIntegration`, raising AttributeError and breaking PR comments entirely on both integrations

[ADVISORY] New error-context behavior is gated on a raw query param (`enable_error_context=false`) with no options entry or feature flag, so operators cannot disable the new nodestore/snuba work per-org or per-region; every request now unconditionally runs an extra Snuba `query_replay_instance` plus a nodestore `get_multi` even when `enable_error_context=false` since the flag only skips `fetch_error_details`, a hot-path regression

[ADVISORY] The new `query_replay_instance` result is used without checking the replay actually exists/is visible — no 404 for a nonexistent replay_id, and `response[0]` is indexed without an empty check, risking IndexError if `process_raw_response` returns a short list; the 404 vs 200-with-empty contract for a missing replay is unstated

[ADVISORY] Unrelated behavior change: default for `autofix_automation_tuning` changes from "low" to "off" in `src/sentry/constants.py:724` and `src/sentry/projectoptions/defaults.py:205`, silently stopping autofix on new issues for default-config orgs

[ADVISORY] Removal of `ParameterizationRegexExperiment` and option `grouping.experiments.parameterization.traceparent` in `parameterization.py:14` and `defaults.py:2627` leaves deployments with that option set referencing an unregistered option, potentially causing errors on option writes

[ADVISORY] Removal of the "Type" row and question tooltips from grouping variant UI in `groupingVariant.tsx:100-136` loses distinct per-type explanatory information with no requirement traceable to this PR

[ADVISORY] constants.py:724 — `DEFAULT_AUTOFIX_AUTOMATION_TUNING_DEFAULT` flips from 'low' to 'off' (mirrored at projectoptions/defaults.py:205) — a customer-visible product behavior change shipped with no feature flag, options entry note, or rollout mechanism, so every org/project relying on the default silently loses automatic autofix on deploy

[ADVISORY] project_replay_summarize_breadcrumbs.py:115-121 — The old `analyze_recording_segments(segments)` produced logs purely from segment events; the new signature prepends `error_events` and interleaves 'User experienced an error...' lines — the summarization contract changed from 'breadcrumbs only' to 'breadcrumbs + errors' as a hidden side effect, so downstream consumers see substantively different output with no spec/version bump and prior summaries cannot be reproduced

[ADVISORY] New `browser_report_validation_failed` logger.warning writes full raw attacker-controlled report body into logs on a CSRF-exempt, unauthenticated, CORS-enabled endpoint, enabling log-injection, PII-in-logs, and log-flooding; the raw_report should at minimum be redacted/truncated

[ADVISORY] Endpoint returns DRF `serializer.errors` (field-level validation details) directly to unauthenticated callers on the new validation path, where prior code returned a bare 422, creating an information disclosure/schema-recon surface

[ADVISORY] commit_context.py:577-593 — merged-PR comment format change (dropped subtitle, added environment, truncation, markdown link move) ships with no updated test pinning the new body; existing tests assert the old format and no tests cover truncation boundary cases (exactly 50, 51 chars, multi-byte titles)

[ADVISORY] project_replay_summarize_breadcrumbs.py:92-118 (get) — new two-phase behavior (full snuba query plus per-error nodestore fetches before pagination, gated by raw query param enable_error_context with no feature flag) has no tests triggering either branch, so a regression breaks replay summarization in production with no test signal

adjudication.rationale: In `BrowserReportSerializer`, both `age` and `timestamp` are declared `required=False`, and the `validate_timestamp`/`validate_age` methods only enforce mutual exclusion when the other field is present (`self.initial_data.get(...)`). There is no validation that *at least one* of `age` or `timestamp` must be provided, so a report with neither will pass `is_valid()` and be processed (added to `validated_reports`) and counted via `metrics.incr(...)` in the endpoint.

adjudication.rationale: Diff shows `BrowserReportSerializer` uses `type = serializers.ChoiceField(choices=BROWSER_REPORT_TYPES)`, so any unrecognized report `type` will be rejected with 422. Also, in `post()`, the loop returns immediately on the first `!serializer.is_valid()`, meaning a single invalid report in the submitted array causes a 422 response for the entire batch (no partial acceptance). However, the claim that Chrome sends omitted types like `nelson` is not verifiable from this diff alone, and whether partial acceptance is required is a product/design choice rather than an inherent correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] `user_agent = serializers.CharField()` is required, but `user_agent` is optional (SHOULD, not MUST) in the editor's draft of the Reporting spec; browsers/proxies that omit it will get 422 where the previous dataclass would have accepted the report, rejecting legitimate report traffic at ingest

adjudication.rationale: In the new `BrowserReportSerializer`, `user_agent = serializers.CharField()` is required. However, in the previous implementation the `BrowserReport` dataclass also had a required `user_agent` field (no default), and the code did `BrowserReport(**report)` inside the loop. If `user_agent` were omitted, dataclass construction would raise a `TypeError` rather than “accepting the report”. So the claim that “the previous dataclass would have accepted the report” is not supported by the diff; the behavior was already incompatible with missing `user_agent` (likely worse, by throwing instead of returning a 422).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] `fetch_error_details` uses `zip(error_ids, events.values())` pairing error IDs positionally with nodestore `get_multi` results, but `get_multi` returns only found nodes; if any node is missing, every subsequent pairing shifts so error ID `X` is reported with event `Y`'s content in the replay summary sent to Seer — must iterate `events[node_id]` per `event_id`

adjudication.rationale: In `fetch_error_details` (src/sentry/replays/endpoints/project_replay_summarize_breadcrumbs.py), the code does `events = nodestore.backend.get_multi(node_ids)` and then builds results with `for event_id, data in zip(error_ids, events.values())`. Since `get_multi` returns a dict keyed by `node_id`, using `.values()` relies on dict iteration order matching `node_ids` and also breaks when some node_ids are missing (the dict may omit missing keys), causing IDs to be paired with the wrong event payloads. This can misreport error details sent to Seer.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] browser_reporting_collector.py:47-60 — age/timestamp mutual-exclusion validators use truthiness, so age=0 or timestamp=0 bypasses the exclusion; and neither field is required, so a report with neither age nor timestamp validates and is accepted with 200 where the previous dataclass would have returned 422, corrupting browser_reporting metrics

This will not flag conflicts when `age=0` or `timestamp=0` (both falsy) even though the field is present. Also, both `age` and `timestamp` are `required=False`, so a payload containing neither will pass validation entirely and be counted in `metrics.incr(...)`, whereas the prior dataclass constructor required `timestamp` and would not accept missing fields. If `get_multi` omits missing keys (common for multi-get APIs) or returns a dict in a different key order, `events.values()` will no longer align with `error_ids`, causing error IDs to be associated with the wrong event payloads and producing an incorrect/garbled error timeline.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] Mutual-exclusion checks in validate_timestamp/validate_age use truthiness so age: 0 or timestamp: 0 passes both validators; use 'age' in self.initial_data instead

adjudication.rationale: In `BrowserReportSerializer`, the mutual-exclusion logic uses truthiness checks: `validate_timestamp` does `if self.initial_data.get("age")` and `validate_age` does `if self.initial_data.get("timestamp")`. This fails when `age: 0` or `timestamp: 0` are explicitly provided, because `0` is falsy, so both validators can incorrectly allow both fields to coexist. The diff shows `timestamp` allows `min_value=0` and `age` is an optional integer, so `0` is a plausible value; the check should be based on key presence (e.g., `'age' in self.initial_data`) rather than truthiness.
